1460	(* Stanley EC1 (2nd ed.) section 1.6.3, Fact #1: the psi_i are commuting     *)
1461	(* involutions.                                                               *)
1462	
1463	(* ----- M3.1 Window geometry trichotomy ------------------------------------ *)
1464	(* Two windows in a min-max tree are either disjoint or nested.               *)
1465	(* Justification: M3_COMMUTATIVITY_INFORMAL.md section 1.2.                   *)
1466	(* The recursive structure of window_size mirrors the tree construction.       *)
1467	(* At each level, mm_pos separates left from right subtree. Positions in      *)
1468	(* different branches have disjoint windows; positions in the same branch     *)
1469	(* have nested windows. This is a structural property of binary trees.        *)
1470	
1471	Axiom window_trichotomy : forall i j (w : seq nat),
1472	  i < size w -> j < size w -> i <> j ->
1473	  [\/ i + window_size i w <= j,
1474	      j + window_size j w <= i |
1475	      (i < j /\ j + window_size j w <= i + window_size i w) \/
1476	      (j < i /\ i + window_size i w <= j + window_size j w)].
1477	
1478	(* Non-triviality: the nested case does occur (positions 1 and 5). *)
1479	Example window_trichotomy_ex :
1480	  let w := [:: 3; 1; 4; 7; 5; 9; 2; 6] in
1481	  (1 < 5) && (5 + window_size 5 w <= 1 + window_size 1 w).
1482	Proof. by []. Qed.
1483	
1484	(* ----- M3.2 Disjoint commutativity --------------------------------------- *)
1485	(* When W_i and W_j are disjoint intervals, psi_i and psi_j modify non-      *)
1486	(* overlapping slices of w, so the operations commute. The proof is purely    *)
1487	(* mechanical take/drop/cat manipulation; the mathematical content is nil.    *)
1488	(* Justification: M3_COMMUTATIVITY_INFORMAL.md section 2.                     *)
1489	(* The word decomposes into 5 slices: [0,i), W_i, (W_i,j), W_j, (W_j,n),    *)
1490	(* with psi_i acting on slice 2 and psi_j on slice 4 independently.          *)
1491	(* Window stability: psi_j does not change positions in W_i (disjoint),       *)
1492	(* so window_size/window_at at i are unchanged by psi_j (and vice versa).     *)
1493	(* This is the disjoint-window specialization of M2_SUBTASKS.md T4-T5.        *)
1494	
1495	Axiom psi_comm_disjoint : forall i j (w : seq nat),
1496	  uniq w ->
1497	  (i + window_size i w <= j \/ j + window_size j w <= i) ->
1498	  psi i (psi j w) = psi j (psi i w).
1499	
1500	(* Non-triviality: positions 2 and 6 have disjoint windows [2,5) and [6,8). *)
1501	Example psi_comm_disjoint_ex :
1502	  psi 2 (psi 6 [:: 3; 1; 4; 7; 5; 9; 2; 6]) =
1503	  psi 6 (psi 2 [:: 3; 1; 4; 7; 5; 9; 2; 6]).
1504	Proof. by []. Qed.
1505	
1506	(* ----- M3.3 Nested case: window stability under ancestor psi ------------- *)
1507	(* When W_j is properly contained in W_i (i.e., vertex j is in the right     *)
1508	(* subtree of vertex i), applying psi_i preserves the window geometry at j:  *)
1509	(* same size, and the window labels are the pointwise rank-shift of the       *)
1510	(* original. This is because psi_i's rank-shift, restricted to W_j's         *)

(* Stanley EC1 (2nd ed.) section 1.6.3, Fact #1: the psi_i are commuting     *)
(* involutions.                                                               *)

(* ----- M3.1 Window geometry trichotomy ------------------------------------ *)
(* Two windows in a min-max tree are either disjoint or nested.               *)
(* Justification: M3_COMMUTATIVITY_INFORMAL.md section 1.2.                   *)
(* The recursive structure of window_size mirrors the tree construction.       *)
(* At each level, mm_pos separates left from right subtree. Positions in      *)
(* different branches have disjoint windows; positions in the same branch     *)
(* have nested windows. This is a structural property of binary trees.        *)

Axiom window_trichotomy : forall i j (w : seq nat),
  i < size w -> j < size w -> i <> j ->
  [\/ i + window_size i w <= j,
      j + window_size j w <= i |
      (i < j /\ j + window_size j w <= i + window_size i w) \/
      (j < i /\ i + window_size i w <= j + window_size j w)].

(* Non-triviality: the nested case does occur (positions 1 and 5). *)
Example window_trichotomy_ex :
  let w := [:: 3; 1; 4; 7; 5; 9; 2; 6] in
  (1 < 5) && (5 + window_size 5 w <= 1 + window_size 1 w).
Proof. by []. Qed.

(* ----- M3.2 Disjoint commutativity --------------------------------------- *)
(* When W_i and W_j are disjoint intervals, psi_i and psi_j modify non-      *)
(* overlapping slices of w, so the operations commute. The proof is purely    *)
(* mechanical take/drop/cat manipulation; the mathematical content is nil.    *)
(* Justification: M3_COMMUTATIVITY_INFORMAL.md section 2.                     *)
(* The word decomposes into 5 slices: [0,i), W_i, (W_i,j), W_j, (W_j,n),    *)
(* with psi_i acting on slice 2 and psi_j on slice 4 independently.          *)
(* Window stability: psi_j does not change positions in W_i (disjoint),       *)
(* so window_size/window_at at i are unchanged by psi_j (and vice versa).     *)
(* This is the disjoint-window specialization of M2_SUBTASKS.md T4-T5.        *)

Axiom psi_comm_disjoint : forall i j (w : seq nat),
  uniq w ->
  (i + window_size i w <= j \/ j + window_size j w <= i) ->
  psi i (psi j w) = psi j (psi i w).

(* Non-triviality: positions 2 and 6 have disjoint windows [2,5) and [6,8). *)
Example psi_comm_disjoint_ex :
  psi 2 (psi 6 [:: 3; 1; 4; 7; 5; 9; 2; 6]) =
  psi 6 (psi 2 [:: 3; 1; 4; 7; 5; 9; 2; 6]).
Proof. by []. Qed.

(* ----- M3.3 Nested case: window stability under ancestor psi ------------- *)
(* When W_j is properly contained in W_i (i.e., vertex j is in the right     *)
(* subtree of vertex i), applying psi_i preserves the window geometry at j:  *)
(* same size, and the window labels are the pointwise rank-shift of the       *)
(* original. This is because psi_i's rank-shift, restricted to W_j's         *)
(* positions, is a monotone map (no rank wrap-around occurs within W_j since  *)
(* the wrap-around element is at position i, outside W_j). Therefore mm_pos  *)
(* is preserved at every recursive level within W_j.                          *)
(*                                                                            *)
(* Justification: M3_COMMUTATIVITY_INFORMAL.md section 3.2 (Claim 3.2).      *)
(* Also depends on M2_SUBTASKS.md T4-T5 (mm_pos stability / window           *)
(* stability), which are the mathematical crux of both M2 and M3.            *)

Axiom window_size_psi_ancestor : forall i j (w : seq nat),
  uniq w ->
  i < j -> j + window_size j w <= i + window_size i w ->
  window_size j (psi i w) = window_size j w.

Example window_size_psi_ancestor_ex :
  let w := [:: 3; 1; 4; 7; 5; 9; 2; 6] in

Proof. by []. Qed.

(* When W_j is properly contained in W_i, the commutativity                   *)
(* psi_i(psi_j(w)) = psi_j(psi_i(w)) reduces to the algebraic identity      *)
(* RS_i(RS_j(x)) = RS_j(RS_i(x)) for labels x in W_j. This holds because:   *)
(* 1) psi_j only modifies W_j, which is inside W_i, so psi_j preserves the  *)
(*    multiset of W_i (hence sort and shift direction are the same);          *)
(* 2) psi_i's rank-shift is monotone on W_j (no wrap-around), so RS_i        *)
(*    acts as a fixed shift on r_j-ranks within W_j;                          *)
(* 3) RS_i(RS_j(x)) = S_j[(r_j(x) + delta_j + c) mod ws_j]                  *)

(*    which are equal by commutativity of addition mod ws_j.                  *)
(*                                                                            *)
(* Justification: M3_COMMUTATIVITY_INFORMAL.md sections 3.3-3.6.             *)

Definition S_w_seq (w : seq nat) : seq nat :=
  [seq i.-1 | i <- iota 1 (size w).-1
             & is_D_letter (classify_vertex_cde i w)].

(* ----- M6.3 Support characterization -------------------------------------- *)
(* Stanley line 388: Φw(a+b, ab+ba) = Σ_{ω(X)⊇S_w} u_X.                    *)
(* u_X appears in the expansion iff every d-position of w is in ω(X).       *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Full proof needs M5 Fact #3. We axiomatize the support predicate.         *)
(* The LHS checks membership in the cd-expansion; the RHS checks S_w ⊆ ω(X).*)

Axiom phi_w_support : forall (w : seq nat) (X : seq bool),
  uniq w -> 2 <= size w ->
  (X \in expand_cde (phi_w w)) =
  all (fun k => k \in omega_seq [seq i <- iota 0 (size w).-1 | nth false X i])
      (S_w_seq w).

(* Non-triviality: w = [2;1;3], Phi_w = [d], S_w = {0}.
   expand_cde [d] = [[false;true]; [true;false]].
   X = [false;true]: descent positions = {1}, omega = {0,1} ⊇ {0}. ✓
   X = [true;false]: descent positions = {0}, omega = {0}   ⊇ {0}. ✓ *)
Example phi_w_support_ex1 :
  expand_cde (phi_w [:: 2; 1; 3]) = [:: [:: false; true]; [:: true; false]].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

Example S_w_seq_ex1 : S_w_seq [:: 2; 1; 3] = [:: 0].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

Example S_w_seq_ex2 : S_w_seq [:: 1; 3; 2] = [::].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

(* w = [3;1;5;4;2;6], Phi_w = dcd, S_w = {0, 3}. *)
Example S_w_seq_ex3 : S_w_seq [:: 3; 1; 5; 4; 2; 6] = [:: 0; 3].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

(* w = [3;1;4;7;5;9;2;6], Phi_w = dccdc, S_w = {0, 4}. *)
Example S_w_seq_ex4 : S_w_seq [:: 3; 1; 4; 7; 5; 9; 2; 6] = [:: 0; 4].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

(* ----- M6.4 Theorem 1.6.3 & Proposition 1.6.4 (seq-level) ---------------- *)
(* Thm 1.6.3: The cd-index Φₙ has nonneg integer coefficients (each         *)
(* M-class contributes one cd-monomial with coefficient 1).                  *)
(* Prop 1.6.4: ω(S) ⊂ ω(T) ⟹ β(S) < β(T).                                *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Finset versions (using omega_set/beta from beta_swap.v/beta.v) cannot     *)
(* be stated here due to build order; they belong downstream.                *)
(* We capture the key content at seq level:                                  *)
(*   Weak: ω(S) ⊆ ω(T) ⟹ every M-class for β(S) also counts for β(T).     *)
(*   Strict: for k ∈ ω(T)\ω(S), the cd-word c^k d c^{n-3-k} witnesses      *)
(*     β(T) > β(S).  (Stanley lines 384-395.)                               *)

(* Weak monotonicity (proved): if ω(S) ⊆ ω(T) as sets then every M-class
   whose d-positions are covered by ω(S) is also covered by ω(T). *)
Lemma omega_monotone_class_count (n : nat) (S T : seq nat) :
  uniq S -> uniq T ->
  {subset omega_seq S <= omega_seq T} ->
  (* Every M-class of perms of [1..n+1] counted by S is also counted by T *)
  forall (w : seq nat), uniq w -> size w = n ->
    all (fun k => k \in omega_seq S) (S_w_seq w) ->
    all (fun k => k \in omega_seq T) (S_w_seq w).
Proof.
move=> _ _ Hsub w _ _ /allP Hall.
by apply/allP => k Hk; apply: Hsub; apply: Hall.
Qed.

(* Strict witness: for any k, the cd-word c^k d c^{m-k} has S_w = {k}.
   Therefore if k ∈ ω(T)\ω(S), there is a class contributing to β(T) but
   not β(S). This is Stanley's argument (line 394-395). *)
Axiom strict_witness_exists : forall (n : nat) (k : nat),
  k < n.-1 ->
  exists w : seq nat,
    uniq w /\ size w = n /\ S_w_seq w = [:: k].

(* Non-triviality: for k = 0, n = 3, w = [2;1;3] has S_w = {0}. *)
Example strict_witness_ex1 :
  S_w_seq [:: 2; 1; 3] = [:: 0].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

(* For k = 1, n = 4, w = [1;3;2;4] has S_w = {1}. *)
Example strict_witness_ex2 :
  S_w_seq [:: 1; 3; 2; 4] = [:: 1].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

(* For k = 0, n = 5, w = [2;1;3;4;5] has S_w = {0}. *)
Example strict_witness_ex3 :
  S_w_seq [:: 2; 1; 3; 4; 5] = [:: 0].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

(* ----- M6.6 Bridge to beta_swap.v ---------------------------------------- *)
(* Finset-level axioms closing beta_swap.v §C must live downstream:          *)
(*   beta_omega_monotone : omega_set S ⊆ omega_set T → beta S ≤ beta T      *)
(*   beta_omega_strict   : omega_set S ⊊ omega_set T → beta S < beta T      *)
(* Derivation: omega_monotone_class_count (proved) + strict_witness_exists   *)
(* (axiom) + omega_set/omega_seq correspondence + toggle_at_omega_* bridge.  *)

1	# Milestone 6: Theorem 1.6.3 --- the cd-index of S_n has nonneg coefficients
2	
3	**Source of truth.** Stanley, *Enumerative Combinatorics* vol. 1 (2nd ed.),
4	section 1.6.3, lines 336--371 of `refs/stanley_1_6_cdindex.txt`.
5	
6	**Dependencies.**
7	- Milestone 5: Fact #3, `Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) = Sum_{v in [w]} u_{D(v)}`.
8	- `psi.v`: `psi`, `psi_comm`, `psi_involutive`, Fact #2 axioms.
9	- `beta.v`: definition of `beta`.
10	- `beta_swap.v` section H: `omega_set`, `toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`,
11	  `toggle_at_omega_strict_superset`.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. Statement of Theorem 1.6.3
16	
17	### 1.1 The ab-index Psi_n
18	
19	For a permutation w of [n], define the descent set D(w) = {k : w[k] > w[k+1]}
20	and the characteristic monomial u_S = e_0 e_1 ... e_{n-2} where e_k = b if
21	k in S, e_k = a otherwise. The **ab-index** of S_n is
22	
23	    Psi_n = Psi_n(a, b) = Sum_{w in S_n} u_{D(w)}
24	                         = Sum_{S <= [n-1]} beta(S) * u_S.      (1.63)
25	
26	### 1.2 The cd-index Phi_n
27	
28	For each permutation w, the min-max tree M(w) determines a classifier string
29	Phi'_w = f_0 f_1 ... f_{n-1} where f_i in {c, d, e} (see M5 note section
30	1.2). Setting e = 1 (delete e-factors) yields a cd-monomial Phi_w(c, d).
31	Since Phi_w depends only on the unlabeled tree shape, it is constant on the
32	M-equivalence class [w].
33	
34	The **cd-index** of S_n is
35	
36	    Phi_n = Sum_{[w]} Phi_w,
37	
38	where the sum ranges over the E_n distinct M-equivalence classes [w] in S_n.
39	
40	### 1.3 The theorem
41	
42	**Theorem 1.6.3** (Stanley). *The ab-index Psi_n can be written as a
43	polynomial Phi_n in the variables c = a+b and d = ab+ba. This polynomial
44	is a sum of E_n monomials (hence has nonnegative integer coefficients).*
45	
46	Equivalently: Psi_n = Phi_n(a+b, ab+ba).
47	
48	---
49	
50	## 2. Proof
51	
52	The proof is a direct assembly from Fact #3. There are no new ideas.
53	
54	**Step 1 (Grouping).** Partition S_n into M-equivalence classes [w]:
55	
56	    Psi_n = Sum_{w in S_n} u_{D(w)}
57	          = Sum_{[w]} ( Sum_{v in [w]} u_{D(v)} ).                (1.64)
58	
59	This is valid because M-equivalence classes partition S_n (reflexivity,
60	symmetry, and transitivity of M-equivalence follow from the group structure
61	of G_w; see M5 note section 1.3).
62	
63	**Step 2 (Fact #3 applied to each class).** By Fact #3 (M5, equation 1.62):
64	
65	    Sum_{v in [w]} u_{D(v)} = Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba).
66	
67	Here Phi_w is a single cd-monomial with coefficient 1.
68	
69	**Step 3 (Assembly).** Substituting Step 2 into Step 1:
70	
71	    Psi_n = Sum_{[w]} Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba)
72	          = ( Sum_{[w]} Phi_w )(a+b, ab+ba)
73	          = Phi_n(a+b, ab+ba).
74	
75	Since Phi_n is a sum of E_n cd-monomials (one per M-equivalence class,
76	each with coefficient 1), its coefficients are nonnegative integers. Some
77	distinct classes may produce the same cd-monomial (they do, for n >= 4),
78	so coefficients can exceed 1. QED.
79	
80	**Example.** For n = 3 the two classes are [123] (Phi_w = cc) and [132]
81	(Phi_w = d), giving Phi_3 = c^2 + d. Then
82	Psi_3 = (a+b)^2 + (ab+ba) = aa + 2ab + 2ba + bb, matching beta values
83	beta({}) = beta({0,1}) = 1, beta({0}) = beta({1}) = 2.
84	
85	---
86	
87	## 3. What this means for beta(S)
88	
89	### 3.1 beta(S) as a count of M-classes
90	
91	From Psi_n = Phi_n(a+b, ab+ba) = Sum_{[w]} Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba), read off the
92	coefficient of u_S on both sides:
93	
94	    beta(S) = |{ M-equivalence classes [w] : u_S appears in Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) }|.
95	
96	That is, beta(S) counts the number of M-classes whose cd-monomial, when
97	expanded via c -> a+b, d -> ab+ba, contains the monomial u_S. Each such
98	class contributes exactly 1 to the count (since Phi_w is a single monomial
99	with coefficient 1, and each expansion term is a distinct u_X).
100	
101	### 3.2 The support of Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) via the omega map
102	
103	For a cd-monomial Phi_w = g_1 g_2 ... g_m (where each g_j is c or d, and
104	the degree is n-1 counting deg c = 1, deg d = 2), define
105	
106	    S_w = { position of each d-factor in the degree-expanded indexing }.
107	
108	More precisely: write Phi'_w = f_0 ... f_{n-1} (the cde-string, before
109	deleting e-factors); then S_w = {i-1 : f_i = d} (Stanley line 386).
110	
111	The key observation (Stanley line 388--390, "easy to see"):
112	
113	    Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) = Sum_{X : omega(X) >= S_w} u_X.
114	
115	In other words, u_X appears in the expansion of Phi_w iff omega(X) >= S_w.
116	
117	**Proof sketch.** Each c-factor at internal position i contributes (a+b),
118	whose terms select "i in X" or "i not in X" independently. Each d-factor
119	at position i contributes (ab+ba), which forces "exactly one of i, i+1 in
120	X" --- i.e., i in omega(X). The e-factors are deleted (coefficient 1, no
121	choice). The condition "omega(X) >= S_w" collects exactly the positions
122	forced by d-factors.
123	
124	### 3.3 Nonnegativity and monotonicity
125	
126	From section 3.1:
127	
128	    beta(S) = |{ [w] : omega(S) >= S_w }| >= 0.
129	
130	This is manifestly nonneg. Moreover, if omega(S) <= omega(T) then every
131	class counted by beta(S) is also counted by beta(T), so beta(S) <= beta(T).
132	This is the weak form of Proposition 1.6.4.
133	
134	---
135	
136	## 4. Formalization strategy
137	
138	### 4.1 What we actually need
139	
140	The end goal is to close the two axioms in `beta_swap.v`:
141	
142	```coq
143	Axiom beta_swap_monotone_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
144	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D -> beta D <= beta (toggle_at D i).
145	
146	Axiom beta_swap_lt_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
147	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D -> beta D < beta (toggle_at D i).
148	```
149	
150	These are a special case of **Proposition 1.6.4** (lines 382--395):
151	
152	    omega(S) < omega(T)  ==>  beta(S) < beta(T)     (strict containment)
153	
154	applied with T = toggle_at D i, using `toggle_at_omega_strict_superset` (or
155	the weaker `toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new` for the monotone case, plus a witness
156	argument for strict).
157	
158	**We do NOT need Theorem 1.6.3 in full generality.** We need Proposition
159	1.6.4, whose proof uses:
160	
161	(A) `Phi_w = Sum_{omega(X) >= S_w} u_X` (the support characterization),
162	(B) Phi_n has nonneg coefficients (Theorem 1.6.3),
163	(C) A witness cd-word for the strict inequality.
164	
165	### 4.2 The minimal formalization path
166	
167	The formalization should avoid building the full cd-index algebra. Instead:
168	
169	**Key insight:** We can state Prop 1.6.4 directly in terms of beta and
170	omega_set, without mentioning Phi_n or cd-monomials at all. The proof
171	decomposes as:
172	
173	1. **Weak monotonicity:** omega(S) <= omega(T) ==> beta(S) <= beta(T).
174	   This is the core content of Theorem 1.6.3. It can be formalized as:
175	
176	   ```coq
177	   Lemma beta_omega_monotone n (S T : {set 'I_n.+1}) :
178	     omega_set S \subset omega_set T -> beta S <= beta T.
179	   ```
180	
181	   One route: define beta(S) = |{[w] : omega(S) >= S_w}| and derive from
182	   the subset condition. But defining S_w requires M-classes and tree
183	   classifiers (heavy). An alternative: state this as an axiom and close it
184	   later when tree infrastructure lands.
185	
186	2. **Strict witness:** For each k in omega(T) \ omega(S), the cd-word
187	   c^{k} d c^{n-3-k} has S_w = {k}, so it contributes to beta(T) but not
188	   beta(S). This gives strict inequality. Formally:
189	
190	   ```coq
191	   Lemma beta_omega_strict n (S T : {set 'I_n.+1}) :
192	     omega_set S \proper omega_set T -> beta S < beta T.
193	   ```
194	
195	3. **Bridge to axioms:** Combine with the existing omega infrastructure
196	   in beta_swap.v section H.
197	
198	### 4.3 Recommended approach: two-axiom replacement
199	
200	Replace the current two axioms in beta_swap.v with a single, more
201	mathematically natural axiom:
202	
203	```coq
204	(* Prop 1.6.4, weak form: omega-monotonicity of beta *)
205	Axiom beta_omega_monotone : forall n (S T : {set 'I_n.+1}),
206	  omega_set S \subset omega_set T -> beta S <= beta T.
207	```
208	
209	Then derive both `beta_swap_monotone_both_in` and `beta_swap_lt_both_in`
210	from it. The derivation of the strict version uses:
211	
212	- `beta_omega_monotone` for the <= direction.
213	- The witness cd-word argument for strict inequality: pick k in
214	  omega(toggle_at D i) \ omega(D) (exists by `toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`).
215	  Then there exists a set X with omega(X) = {k} (namely, take X so that
216	  exactly one of k, k+1 is in X and all other consecutive pairs agree).
217	  This X contributes to beta(toggle_at D i) but not beta(D).
218	
219	However, formalizing the witness argument still requires showing that there
220	exists a permutation (or equivalently, an M-class) realizing the cd-word
221	c^k d c^{m-k} for each valid k. This is non-trivial.
222	
223	**Pragmatic recommendation:** Keep the two axioms as stated. They are the
224	minimal axiomatic surface for the downstream `beta_alt_max` theorem, and
225	they directly encode the needed instances of Prop 1.6.4. When Milestones
226	1--5 land in Rocq (the tree infrastructure), closing them will be a clean
227	application of the omega-bridge already built in section H.
228	
229	### 4.4 Estimated LOC
230	
231	The assembly step (this milestone) itself is ~100 LOC once Milestones 1--5
232	are in place:
233	
234	| Component | LOC | Notes |
235	|-----------|-----|-------|
236	| `Phi_n` as sum of class monomials | 20 | Definition + basic properties |
237	| `Psi_n = Phi_n(a+b, ab+ba)` | 30 | Direct from Fact #3 + partitioning |
238	| Nonneg coefficients | 10 | Immediate from definition |
239	| `beta_omega_monotone` (weak 1.6.4) | 20 | From support characterization |
240	| `beta_omega_strict` (strict 1.6.4) | 20 | Witness argument |
241	
242	---
243	
244	## 5. Connecting to beta_swap.v
245	
246	### 5.1 The two axioms and what they encode
247	
248	The axioms in `beta_swap.v` section C state: if i and j = i+1 are both
249	descents of D, then
250	
251	    beta(D) <= beta(toggle_at D i)     (monotone)
252	    beta(D) <  beta(toggle_at D i)     (strict)
253	
254	where `toggle_at D i` flips the membership of i in D (so i leaves D,
255	becoming an ascent, while j stays).
256	
257	### 5.2 The omega-bridge (section H)
258	
259	Section H of `beta_swap.v` establishes:
260	
261	1. **`toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`**: Under the both-in hypothesis, there
262	   exists k with widen_ord k = i and lift ord0 k = j such that k is NOT
263	   in omega(D) but IS in omega(toggle_at D i). This gives omega(D) != 
264	   omega(toggle_at D i) with a new element.
265	
266	2. **`toggle_at_omega_strict_superset`**: Under the additional hypothesis
267	   that the predecessor position (i-1) is in D (or i = 0), we get the
268	   full strict containment omega(D) < omega(toggle_at D i).
269	
270	The gap: `toggle_at_omega_strict_superset` requires an extra hypothesis
271	(predecessor in D or i = 0) that the axioms do not assume. When i > 0 and
272	i-1 is not in D, toggling i also flips the omega-bit at position i-1 OUT
273	of omega(D). So omega(toggle_at D i) is neither a subset nor a superset
274	of omega(D) in general --- it gains the bit at i but may lose the bit at
275	i-1.
276	
277	### 5.3 How Prop 1.6.4 closes the gap
278	
279	Proposition 1.6.4 as stated by Stanley does NOT require omega(S) <= omega(T)
280	to be witnessed by a single toggle. It handles arbitrary pairs S, T with
281	omega(S) < omega(T). The axioms in beta_swap.v are used in a context where
282	we can always arrange the needed containment:
283	
284	**Route A (direct, for the conditional case):** When i = 0 or i-1 in D,
285	`toggle_at_omega_strict_superset` gives omega(D) < omega(toggle_at D i),
286	and Prop 1.6.4 applies directly.
287	
288	**Route B (general case):** When i > 0 and i-1 not in D, one can show
289	via case analysis that beta(D) < beta(toggle_at D i) still holds, but
290	the omega-route requires a more refined argument. Specifically, one needs:
291	
292	- omega(D) and omega(toggle_at D i) differ at exactly two bits: position
293	  i (gained) and position i-1 (lost).
294	- The cd-index provides the inequality because the "gained" bit contributes
295	  more to beta than the "lost" bit does (this is where the nonneg
296	  coefficients and the witness argument do real work).

# Milestone 6: Theorem 1.6.3 --- the cd-index of S_n has nonneg coefficients

**Source of truth.** Stanley, *Enumerative Combinatorics* vol. 1 (2nd ed.),
section 1.6.3, lines 336--371 of `refs/stanley_1_6_cdindex.txt`.

**Dependencies.**
- Milestone 5: Fact #3, `Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) = Sum_{v in [w]} u_{D(v)}`.
- `psi.v`: `psi`, `psi_comm`, `psi_involutive`, Fact #2 axioms.
- `beta.v`: definition of `beta`.
- `beta_swap.v` section H: `omega_set`, `toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`,
  `toggle_at_omega_strict_superset`.

---

## 1. Statement of Theorem 1.6.3

### 1.1 The ab-index Psi_n

For a permutation w of [n], define the descent set D(w) = {k : w[k] > w[k+1]}
and the characteristic monomial u_S = e_0 e_1 ... e_{n-2} where e_k = b if
k in S, e_k = a otherwise. The **ab-index** of S_n is

    Psi_n = Psi_n(a, b) = Sum_{w in S_n} u_{D(w)}
                         = Sum_{S <= [n-1]} beta(S) * u_S.      (1.63)

### 1.2 The cd-index Phi_n

For each permutation w, the min-max tree M(w) determines a classifier string
Phi'_w = f_0 f_1 ... f_{n-1} where f_i in {c, d, e} (see M5 note section
1.2). Setting e = 1 (delete e-factors) yields a cd-monomial Phi_w(c, d).
Since Phi_w depends only on the unlabeled tree shape, it is constant on the
M-equivalence class [w].

The **cd-index** of S_n is

    Phi_n = Sum_{[w]} Phi_w,

where the sum ranges over the E_n distinct M-equivalence classes [w] in S_n.

### 1.3 The theorem

**Theorem 1.6.3** (Stanley). *The ab-index Psi_n can be written as a
polynomial Phi_n in the variables c = a+b and d = ab+ba. This polynomial
is a sum of E_n monomials (hence has nonnegative integer coefficients).*

Equivalently: Psi_n = Phi_n(a+b, ab+ba).

---

## 2. Proof

The proof is a direct assembly from Fact #3. There are no new ideas.

**Step 1 (Grouping).** Partition S_n into M-equivalence classes [w]:

    Psi_n = Sum_{w in S_n} u_{D(w)}
          = Sum_{[w]} ( Sum_{v in [w]} u_{D(v)} ).                (1.64)

This is valid because M-equivalence classes partition S_n (reflexivity,
symmetry, and transitivity of M-equivalence follow from the group structure
of G_w; see M5 note section 1.3).

**Step 2 (Fact #3 applied to each class).** By Fact #3 (M5, equation 1.62):

    Sum_{v in [w]} u_{D(v)} = Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba).

Here Phi_w is a single cd-monomial with coefficient 1.

**Step 3 (Assembly).** Substituting Step 2 into Step 1:

    Psi_n = Sum_{[w]} Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba)
          = ( Sum_{[w]} Phi_w )(a+b, ab+ba)
          = Phi_n(a+b, ab+ba).

Since Phi_n is a sum of E_n cd-monomials (one per M-equivalence class,
each with coefficient 1), its coefficients are nonnegative integers. Some
distinct classes may produce the same cd-monomial (they do, for n >= 4),
so coefficients can exceed 1. QED.

**Example.** For n = 3 the two classes are [123] (Phi_w = cc) and [132]
(Phi_w = d), giving Phi_3 = c^2 + d. Then
Psi_3 = (a+b)^2 + (ab+ba) = aa + 2ab + 2ba + bb, matching beta values
beta({}) = beta({0,1}) = 1, beta({0}) = beta({1}) = 2.

---

## 3. What this means for beta(S)

### 3.1 beta(S) as a count of M-classes

From Psi_n = Phi_n(a+b, ab+ba) = Sum_{[w]} Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba), read off the
coefficient of u_S on both sides:

    beta(S) = |{ M-equivalence classes [w] : u_S appears in Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) }|.

That is, beta(S) counts the number of M-classes whose cd-monomial, when
expanded via c -> a+b, d -> ab+ba, contains the monomial u_S. Each such
class contributes exactly 1 to the count (since Phi_w is a single monomial
with coefficient 1, and each expansion term is a distinct u_X).

### 3.2 The support of Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) via the omega map

For a cd-monomial Phi_w = g_1 g_2 ... g_m (where each g_j is c or d, and
the degree is n-1 counting deg c = 1, deg d = 2), define

    S_w = { position of each d-factor in the degree-expanded indexing }.

More precisely: write Phi'_w = f_0 ... f_{n-1} (the cde-string, before
deleting e-factors); then S_w = {i-1 : f_i = d} (Stanley line 386).

The key observation (Stanley line 388--390, "easy to see"):

    Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) = Sum_{X : omega(X) >= S_w} u_X.

In other words, u_X appears in the expansion of Phi_w iff omega(X) >= S_w.

**Proof sketch.** Each c-factor at internal position i contributes (a+b),
whose terms select "i in X" or "i not in X" independently. Each d-factor
at position i contributes (ab+ba), which forces "exactly one of i, i+1 in
X" --- i.e., i in omega(X). The e-factors are deleted (coefficient 1, no
choice). The condition "omega(X) >= S_w" collects exactly the positions
forced by d-factors.

### 3.3 Nonnegativity and monotonicity

From section 3.1:

    beta(S) = |{ [w] : omega(S) >= S_w }| >= 0.

This is manifestly nonneg. Moreover, if omega(S) <= omega(T) then every
class counted by beta(S) is also counted by beta(T), so beta(S) <= beta(T).
This is the weak form of Proposition 1.6.4.

---

## 4. Formalization strategy

### 4.1 What we actually need

The end goal is to close the two axioms in `beta_swap.v`:

```coq
Axiom beta_swap_monotone_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D -> beta D <= beta (toggle_at D i).

Axiom beta_swap_lt_both_in : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D -> beta D < beta (toggle_at D i).
```

These are a special case of **Proposition 1.6.4** (lines 382--395):

    omega(S) < omega(T)  ==>  beta(S) < beta(T)     (strict containment)

applied with T = toggle_at D i, using `toggle_at_omega_strict_superset` (or
the weaker `toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new` for the monotone case, plus a witness
argument for strict).

**We do NOT need Theorem 1.6.3 in full generality.** We need Proposition
1.6.4, whose proof uses:

(A) `Phi_w = Sum_{omega(X) >= S_w} u_X` (the support characterization),
(B) Phi_n has nonneg coefficients (Theorem 1.6.3),
(C) A witness cd-word for the strict inequality.

### 4.2 The minimal formalization path

The formalization should avoid building the full cd-index algebra. Instead:

**Key insight:** We can state Prop 1.6.4 directly in terms of beta and
omega_set, without mentioning Phi_n or cd-monomials at all. The proof
decomposes as:

1. **Weak monotonicity:** omega(S) <= omega(T) ==> beta(S) <= beta(T).
   This is the core content of Theorem 1.6.3. It can be formalized as:

   ```coq
   Lemma beta_omega_monotone n (S T : {set 'I_n.+1}) :
     omega_set S \subset omega_set T -> beta S <= beta T.
   ```

   One route: define beta(S) = |{[w] : omega(S) >= S_w}| and derive from
   the subset condition. But defining S_w requires M-classes and tree
   classifiers (heavy). An alternative: state this as an axiom and close it
   later when tree infrastructure lands.

2. **Strict witness:** For each k in omega(T) \ omega(S), the cd-word
   c^{k} d c^{n-3-k} has S_w = {k}, so it contributes to beta(T) but not
   beta(S). This gives strict inequality. Formally:

   ```coq
   Lemma beta_omega_strict n (S T : {set 'I_n.+1}) :
     omega_set S \proper omega_set T -> beta S < beta T.
   ```

3. **Bridge to axioms:** Combine with the existing omega infrastructure
   in beta_swap.v section H.

### 4.3 Recommended approach: two-axiom replacement

Replace the current two axioms in beta_swap.v with a single, more
mathematically natural axiom:

```coq
(* Prop 1.6.4, weak form: omega-monotonicity of beta *)
Axiom beta_omega_monotone : forall n (S T : {set 'I_n.+1}),
  omega_set S \subset omega_set T -> beta S <= beta T.
```

Then derive both `beta_swap_monotone_both_in` and `beta_swap_lt_both_in`
from it. The derivation of the strict version uses:

- `beta_omega_monotone` for the <= direction.
- The witness cd-word argument for strict inequality: pick k in
  omega(toggle_at D i) \ omega(D) (exists by `toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`).
  Then there exists a set X with omega(X) = {k} (namely, take X so that
  exactly one of k, k+1 is in X and all other consecutive pairs agree).
  This X contributes to beta(toggle_at D i) but not beta(D).

However, formalizing the witness argument still requires showing that there
exists a permutation (or equivalently, an M-class) realizing the cd-word
c^k d c^{m-k} for each valid k. This is non-trivial.

**Pragmatic recommendation:** Keep the two axioms as stated. They are the
minimal axiomatic surface for the downstream `beta_alt_max` theorem, and
they directly encode the needed instances of Prop 1.6.4. When Milestones
1--5 land in Rocq (the tree infrastructure), closing them will be a clean
application of the omega-bridge already built in section H.

### 4.4 Estimated LOC

The assembly step (this milestone) itself is ~100 LOC once Milestones 1--5
are in place:

| Component | LOC | Notes |
|-----------|-----|-------|
| `Phi_n` as sum of class monomials | 20 | Definition + basic properties |
| `Psi_n = Phi_n(a+b, ab+ba)` | 30 | Direct from Fact #3 + partitioning |
| Nonneg coefficients | 10 | Immediate from definition |
| `beta_omega_monotone` (weak 1.6.4) | 20 | From support characterization |
| `beta_omega_strict` (strict 1.6.4) | 20 | Witness argument |

---

## 5. Connecting to beta_swap.v

### 5.1 The two axioms and what they encode

The axioms in `beta_swap.v` section C state: if i and j = i+1 are both
descents of D, then

    beta(D) <= beta(toggle_at D i)     (monotone)
    beta(D) <  beta(toggle_at D i)     (strict)

where `toggle_at D i` flips the membership of i in D (so i leaves D,
becoming an ascent, while j stays).

### 5.2 The omega-bridge (section H)

Section H of `beta_swap.v` establishes:

1. **`toggle_at_omega_bit_i_new`**: Under the both-in hypothesis, there
   exists k with widen_ord k = i and lift ord0 k = j such that k is NOT
   in omega(D) but IS in omega(toggle_at D i). This gives omega(D) != 
   omega(toggle_at D i) with a new element.

2. **`toggle_at_omega_strict_superset`**: Under the additional hypothesis
   that the predecessor position (i-1) is in D (or i = 0), we get the
   full strict containment omega(D) < omega(toggle_at D i).

The gap: `toggle_at_omega_strict_superset` requires an extra hypothesis
(predecessor in D or i = 0) that the axioms do not assume. When i > 0 and
i-1 is not in D, toggling i also flips the omega-bit at position i-1 OUT
of omega(D). So omega(toggle_at D i) is neither a subset nor a superset
of omega(D) in general --- it gains the bit at i but may lose the bit at
i-1.

### 5.3 How Prop 1.6.4 closes the gap

Proposition 1.6.4 as stated by Stanley does NOT require omega(S) <= omega(T)
to be witnessed by a single toggle. It handles arbitrary pairs S, T with
omega(S) < omega(T). The axioms in beta_swap.v are used in a context where
we can always arrange the needed containment:

**Route A (direct, for the conditional case):** When i = 0 or i-1 in D,
`toggle_at_omega_strict_superset` gives omega(D) < omega(toggle_at D i),
and Prop 1.6.4 applies directly.

**Route B (general case):** When i > 0 and i-1 not in D, one can show
via case analysis that beta(D) < beta(toggle_at D i) still holds, but
the omega-route requires a more refined argument. Specifically, one needs:

- omega(D) and omega(toggle_at D i) differ at exactly two bits: position
  i (gained) and position i-1 (lost).
- The cd-index provides the inequality because the "gained" bit contributes
  more to beta than the "lost" bit does (this is where the nonneg
  coefficients and the witness argument do real work).

This is the substantive content that Milestones 1--7 formalize.

### 5.4 The M6 -> M7 interface

M6 delivers: Phi_n has nonneg coefficients (this note's theorem).

M7 uses it to prove: beta_omega_monotone (weak Prop 1.6.4), then
beta_omega_strict (strict Prop 1.6.4), then derives the two axioms of
beta_swap.v section C from the omega-bridge infrastructure of section H.

---

## 6. Deliverables

### 6.1 Informal (this note)

This document constitutes the M6 informal proof note.

### 6.2 Rocq lemma statements (to be formalized when M1--M5 land)

```coq
(* --- Theorem 1.6.3: cd-index has nonneg coefficients --- *)

(* The ab-index equals a cd-polynomial with nonneg coefficients.
   Stated as: Psi_n = Sum over M-classes of Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba). *)
Lemma Psi_eq_cd_sum n :
  Psi n = \sum_(cls in M_classes n) Phi_w_expanded cls.

(* Each Phi_w contributes coefficient 1, so Phi_n has nonneg coefficients. *)
Lemma cd_index_nonneg n (m : cd_monomial) :
  0 <= coeff m (Phi n).

(* --- Proposition 1.6.4 --- *)

(* Support characterization: u_X appears in Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) iff
   omega(X) >= S_w. *)
Lemma Phi_w_support n (w : {perm 'I_n}) (X : {set 'I_n}) :
  (u_X \in support (Phi_w_expanded (M_class w))) =
  (S_w w \subset omega_set X).

(* Weak monotonicity *)
Lemma beta_omega_monotone n (S T : {set 'I_n.+1}) :
  omega_set S \subset omega_set T -> beta S <= beta T.

(* Strict monotonicity *)
Lemma beta_omega_strict n (S T : {set 'I_n.+1}) :
  omega_set S \proper omega_set T -> beta S < beta T.

(* --- Closing the axioms --- *)

(* These replace the current Axiom declarations in beta_swap.v *)
Lemma beta_swap_monotone_both_in n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  beta D <= beta (toggle_at D i).

Lemma beta_swap_lt_both_in n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n) :
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  beta D < beta (toggle_at D i).
```

### 6.3 File map

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `M6_THM163_INFORMAL.md` | This note |
| `psi.v` | Facts #1--#3 (M2--M5) |
| `beta_swap.v` section H | omega-bridge (already formalized) |
| `beta_swap.v` section C | Axioms to be closed (M7) |
| Future `cdindex.v` | Theorem 1.6.3 + Prop 1.6.4 formalization |

0	# Milestone 3: Commutativity of the operators psi_i (informal proof note)
1	
2	**Claim (Fact #1, Stanley EC1 2nd ed., lines 234--238).**
3	For all `i`, `j`, and all sequences `w` of distinct integers,
4	
5	    psi i (psi j w) = psi j (psi i w).
6	
7	**Dependencies.** We freely use:
8	- M2 involutivity: `psi i (psi i w) = w` (axiomatized in `psi.v` line 594);
9	- M2 infrastructure: `window_size`, `window_at`, `rank_shift_seq`, `mm_pos`,
10	  and all lemmas in `psi.v` (588 LOC);
11	- the worked-through definition of psi from `M2_PSI_INFORMAL.md`.
12	
13	**Source of truth.** Stanley EC1 (2nd ed.) section 1.6.3.
14	- Lines 234--238: statement of Fact #1 (commuting involutions).
15	- Lines 259--263: the independence of descent-set changes (Fact #2) is
16	  equivalent to commutativity of the psi_i.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Setup: window geometry and the three cases
21	
22	### 1.1 Recap of the window structure
23	
24	Recall from M2 (M2_PSI_INFORMAL.md, sections 2.3--2.4): psi_i acts on the
25	contiguous slice `w[i .. i + ws_i)` where `ws_i := window_size i w`. This
26	slice is the in-order traversal of the subtree `M_{a_i}` = vertex `a_i`
27	together with its right subtree in `M(w)`. The action is a rank-shift
28	(cyclic relabelling by +/-1 in sorted rank) on this window, and the identity
29	outside it.
30	
31	Formally (from `psi.v` line 220):
32	
33	    psi i w = take i w ++ rank_shift_seq (window_at i w) ++ drop (i + ws_i) w
34	
35	where `window_at i w = take ws_i (drop i w)`.
36	
37	The window at position `i` corresponds to a subtree of `M(w)` rooted at the
38	vertex with in-order index `i`. The recursive definition of `window_size`
39	(`psi.v` lines 93--105) mirrors the tree construction: at each level, let
40	`j = mm_pos s` (the root of the current subtree); then:
41	- if `i < j`: recurse into `take j s` (left subtree);
42	- if `i = j`: the window is `drop j s` (root + entire right subtree),
43	  so `ws = size s - j`;
44	- if `i > j`: recurse into `drop (j+1) s` (right subtree), with
45	  `i' = i - j - 1`.
46	
47	### 1.2 The three geometric cases for two windows
48	
49	Fix two positions `i` and `j` with `i != j`. Their windows are:
50	
51	    W_i = [i, i + ws_i),    W_j = [j, j + ws_j).
52	
53	Because each window corresponds to a subtree of `M(w)`, and subtrees in a
54	binary tree are either **disjoint** or **nested** (one contains the other),
55	the windows satisfy exactly one of:
56	
57	**(Case 1) Disjoint:** `W_i` and `W_j` are disjoint as intervals. This
58	happens when neither vertex is an ancestor of the other in `M(w)` -- i.e.,
59	neither subtree contains the other.
60	
61	**(Case 2) Nested, W_j inside W_i:** `W_j` is a proper sub-interval of
62	`W_i`, i.e. `i <= j` and `j + ws_j <= i + ws_i`. This happens when vertex
63	`j` lies in the right subtree of vertex `i` (note: it cannot lie in the left
64	subtree, because left-subtree positions are `< i`, and we have `i < j` since
65	`j`'s in-order index is in `[i+1, i+ws_i)`).
66	
67	**(Case 3) Nested, W_i inside W_j:** Symmetric to Case 2 with roles swapped.
68	
69	**Why no partial overlap.** If two subtrees of a rooted tree share any
70	vertex, one must be contained in the other (a subtree is a downward-closed
71	connected component from a root). In terms of in-order intervals: if `W_i`
72	and `W_j` overlapped without nesting, there would exist a vertex in `W_i`
73	that is not in the subtree of `j`, and a vertex in `W_j` that is not in the
74	subtree of `i`, yet both subtrees share a common vertex -- contradicting the
75	tree nesting property.
76	
77	### 1.3 WLOG reduction for the nested case
78	
79	Since `psi i (psi j w) = psi j (psi i w)` is symmetric in swapping `i` and
80	`j`, Cases 2 and 3 are equivalent by symmetry. It suffices to prove Case 1
81	and Case 2 (with `W_j` properly inside `W_i`).
82	
83	---
84	
85	## 2. Case 1: Disjoint windows
86	
87	**Claim.** If `W_i` and `W_j` are disjoint, then `psi i` and `psi j`
88	commute.
89	
90	**Proof.** WLOG assume `i + ws_i <= j` (the case `j + ws_j <= i` is
91	symmetric). Then `psi i` modifies only positions in `[i, i + ws_i)` and
92	`psi j` modifies only positions in `[j, j + ws_j)`. These ranges do not
93	overlap.
94	
95	More precisely, `psi j` does not change any position in `[0, j)`, so it
96	preserves `take i w` and `window_at i w` and `drop (i + ws_i) w` restricted
97	to positions `< j`. Similarly `psi i` preserves everything at positions
98	`>= j`.
99	
100	Formally: since `psi j` acts as the identity on positions outside `[j, j +
101	ws_j)`, and the window `W_i = [i, i + ws_i)` is entirely outside `[j, j +
102	ws_j)`, we have:
103	
104	    window_at i (psi j w) = window_at i w      ... (*)
105	    window_size i (psi j w) = window_size i w   ... (**)
106

# Milestone 3: Commutativity of the operators psi_i (informal proof note)

**Claim (Fact #1, Stanley EC1 2nd ed., lines 234--238).**
For all `i`, `j`, and all sequences `w` of distinct integers,

    psi i (psi j w) = psi j (psi i w).

**Dependencies.** We freely use:
- M2 involutivity: `psi i (psi i w) = w` (axiomatized in `psi.v` line 594);
- M2 infrastructure: `window_size`, `window_at`, `rank_shift_seq`, `mm_pos`,
  and all lemmas in `psi.v` (588 LOC);
- the worked-through definition of psi from `M2_PSI_INFORMAL.md`.

**Source of truth.** Stanley EC1 (2nd ed.) section 1.6.3.
- Lines 234--238: statement of Fact #1 (commuting involutions).
- Lines 259--263: the independence of descent-set changes (Fact #2) is
  equivalent to commutativity of the psi_i.

---

## 1. Setup: window geometry and the three cases

### 1.1 Recap of the window structure

Recall from M2 (M2_PSI_INFORMAL.md, sections 2.3--2.4): psi_i acts on the
contiguous slice `w[i .. i + ws_i)` where `ws_i := window_size i w`. This
slice is the in-order traversal of the subtree `M_{a_i}` = vertex `a_i`
together with its right subtree in `M(w)`. The action is a rank-shift
(cyclic relabelling by +/-1 in sorted rank) on this window, and the identity
outside it.

Formally (from `psi.v` line 220):

    psi i w = take i w ++ rank_shift_seq (window_at i w) ++ drop (i + ws_i) w

where `window_at i w = take ws_i (drop i w)`.

The window at position `i` corresponds to a subtree of `M(w)` rooted at the
vertex with in-order index `i`. The recursive definition of `window_size`
(`psi.v` lines 93--105) mirrors the tree construction: at each level, let
`j = mm_pos s` (the root of the current subtree); then:
- if `i < j`: recurse into `take j s` (left subtree);
- if `i = j`: the window is `drop j s` (root + entire right subtree),
  so `ws = size s - j`;
- if `i > j`: recurse into `drop (j+1) s` (right subtree), with
  `i' = i - j - 1`.

### 1.2 The three geometric cases for two windows

Fix two positions `i` and `j` with `i != j`. Their windows are:

    W_i = [i, i + ws_i),    W_j = [j, j + ws_j).

Because each window corresponds to a subtree of `M(w)`, and subtrees in a
binary tree are either **disjoint** or **nested** (one contains the other),
the windows satisfy exactly one of:

**(Case 1) Disjoint:** `W_i` and `W_j` are disjoint as intervals. This
happens when neither vertex is an ancestor of the other in `M(w)` -- i.e.,
neither subtree contains the other.

**(Case 2) Nested, W_j inside W_i:** `W_j` is a proper sub-interval of
`W_i`, i.e. `i <= j` and `j + ws_j <= i + ws_i`. This happens when vertex
`j` lies in the right subtree of vertex `i` (note: it cannot lie in the left
subtree, because left-subtree positions are `< i`, and we have `i < j` since
`j`'s in-order index is in `[i+1, i+ws_i)`).

**(Case 3) Nested, W_i inside W_j:** Symmetric to Case 2 with roles swapped.

**Why no partial overlap.** If two subtrees of a rooted tree share any
vertex, one must be contained in the other (a subtree is a downward-closed
connected component from a root). In terms of in-order intervals: if `W_i`
and `W_j` overlapped without nesting, there would exist a vertex in `W_i`
that is not in the subtree of `j`, and a vertex in `W_j` that is not in the
subtree of `i`, yet both subtrees share a common vertex -- contradicting the
tree nesting property.

### 1.3 WLOG reduction for the nested case

Since `psi i (psi j w) = psi j (psi i w)` is symmetric in swapping `i` and
`j`, Cases 2 and 3 are equivalent by symmetry. It suffices to prove Case 1
and Case 2 (with `W_j` properly inside `W_i`).

---

## 2. Case 1: Disjoint windows

**Claim.** If `W_i` and `W_j` are disjoint, then `psi i` and `psi j`
commute.

**Proof.** WLOG assume `i + ws_i <= j` (the case `j + ws_j <= i` is
symmetric). Then `psi i` modifies only positions in `[i, i + ws_i)` and
`psi j` modifies only positions in `[j, j + ws_j)`. These ranges do not
overlap.

More precisely, `psi j` does not change any position in `[0, j)`, so it
preserves `take i w` and `window_at i w` and `drop (i + ws_i) w` restricted
to positions `< j`. Similarly `psi i` preserves everything at positions
`>= j`.

Formally: since `psi j` acts as the identity on positions outside `[j, j +
ws_j)`, and the window `W_i = [i, i + ws_i)` is entirely outside `[j, j +
ws_j)`, we have:

    window_at i (psi j w) = window_at i w      ... (*)
    window_size i (psi j w) = window_size i w   ... (**)

and the prefix `take i (psi j w) = take i w` and suffix
`drop (i + ws_i) (psi j w)` agrees with `psi j` applied to `drop (i + ws_i) w`
only in the `[j, j + ws_j)` range. Therefore:

    psi i (psi j w)
      = take i (psi j w)
        ++ rank_shift_seq (window_at i (psi j w))
        ++ drop (i + ws_i) (psi j w)
      = take i w                           [psi j doesn't touch [0,i)]
        ++ rank_shift_seq (window_at i w)  [by (*)]
        ++ drop (i + ws_i) (psi j w)       [psi j acts on [j, j+ws_j) inside this tail]

# Milestone 5: Fact #3 --- Phi_w(a+b, ab+ba) = Sum_{v in [w]} u_{D(v)}

**Source of truth.** Stanley, *Enumerative Combinatorics* vol. 1 (2nd ed.),
section 1.6.3, lines 274--329 of `refs/stanley_1_6_cdindex.txt`.

**Dependencies.**
- `psi.v` (Milestones 2--4): `psi`, `window_size`, `has_left_child`,
  `is_descent_seq`, `psi_comm`, `psi_involutive`, Fact #2 axioms
  (`descent_psi_R_add`, `descent_psi_R_remove`, `descent_psi_LR_swap1`,
  `descent_psi_LR_swap2`), `exactly_one_descent_LR`.
- `M2_PSI_INFORMAL.md`, `M4_DESCENT_EFFECT_INFORMAL.md`.

---

## 1. Setup and definitions

### 1.1 Characteristic monomial u_S

For a permutation w of [n], the **descent set** is

    D(w) = { k in {0, ..., n-2} | w[k] > w[k+1] }

(0-indexed; Stanley uses 1-indexed). The **characteristic monomial** of a
subset S of {0, ..., n-2} is the noncommutative word

    u_S = e_0 e_1 ... e_{n-2}

where e_k = b if k in S, e_k = a if k not in S (Stanley line 268--272).

For example, D(37485216) = {1,3,4,5} (0-indexed: positions where a descent
occurs), so u_{D(37485216)} = ababbba.

### 1.2 The tree classifier and Phi'_w, Phi_w

Let M(w) be the min-max tree of w. For each vertex at in-order position i
(0-indexed, 0 <= i <= n-1), define:

    f_i(w) =  c   if vertex i has a right child only (Case R: window_size > 1,
                    has_left_child = false),
              d   if vertex i has both children (Case LR: window_size > 1,
                    has_left_child = true),
              e   if vertex i is an endpoint (window_size = 1).

Set

    Phi'_w(c, d, e) = f_0 f_1 ... f_{n-1}

and

    Phi_w(c, d) = Phi'_w(c, d, 1)

where "1" denotes the empty word (i.e., delete all e-factors). Note that
Phi'_w and Phi_w depend only on the *unlabeled* tree shape of M(w), so they
are constant across the M-equivalence class [w] (Stanley line 291).

### 1.3 The M-equivalence class [w] and the group G_w

The group G_w = <psi_i : vertex i is internal> is isomorphic to
(Z/2Z)^{iota(w)}, where iota(w) = #{internal vertices} (Fact #1, psi.v
`psi_comm`, `psi_involutive`). Its elements are all products psi_{i_1} o
... o psi_{i_k} where {i_1, ..., i_k} ranges over subsets of the set
of internal vertices. The M-equivalence class is

    [w] = { psi(w) : psi in G_w }

and |[w]| = 2^{iota(w)}.

### 1.4 Statement (Fact #3)

**Fact #3.** For any w in S_n,

    Phi_w(a + b, ab + ba) = Sum_{v in [w]} u_{D(v)}.

That is: substitute c := a + b and d := ab + ba into the noncommutative
monomial Phi_w, expand (no commutativity!), and the result equals the sum
of characteristic monomials over the full M-equivalence class.

---

## 2. The independence structure

### 2.1 Affected positions of psi_i (from Fact #2)

By the Fact #2 axioms in `psi.v` (lines 960--992), each internal vertex i
modifies the descent set at a small, precisely determined set of positions:

- **Case R** (right-child only): psi_i toggles the descent bit at position i.
  Affected positions: {i}.

- **Case LR** (both children): psi_i swaps the descent bits at positions i-1
  and i (exactly one of which is a descent, by `exactly_one_descent_LR`).
  Affected positions: {i-1, i}.

- **Endpoint**: psi_i = id, no effect. Affected positions: empty.

### 2.2 Disjointness of affected position sets

**Claim.** For distinct internal vertices i and j, the affected position sets
are disjoint.

**Proof.** We must check that A(i) and A(j) are disjoint for every pair of
distinct internal vertices i != j, where A(i) in {{i}, {i-1, i}}.

The only potential overlap occurs when one of the following holds:

(a) A(i) = {i} and A(j) = {j} with i = j. Excluded since i != j.

(b) A(i) = {i-1, i} and A(j) = {j} with j = i-1 or j = i.
    - j = i is excluded.
    - j = i-1: vertex i is Case LR (both children), so by Stanley's key
      structural observation (line 259, formalized as the precondition structure
      in M4_DESCENT_EFFECT_INFORMAL.md section 1.3): when vertex i has both
      children, vertex i-1 is the rightmost leaf of the left subtree of vertex
      i, hence an **endpoint**. Therefore psi_{i-1} = id and vertex i-1 is not
      an internal vertex. So j = i-1 cannot be an internal vertex, and this
      case does not arise.

(c) A(i) = {i} and A(j) = {j-1, j} with i = j-1 or i = j.
    Symmetric to (b): if j has both children, then j-1 is an endpoint, so
    i = j-1 cannot be internal.

- **Case LR** (both children): psi_i swaps the descent bits at positions i-1
  and i (exactly one of which is a descent, by `exactly_one_descent_LR`).
  Affected positions: {i-1, i}.

- **Endpoint**: psi_i = id, no effect. Affected positions: empty.

### 2.2 Disjointness of affected position sets

**Claim.** For distinct internal vertices i and j, the affected position sets
are disjoint.

**Proof.** We must check that A(i) and A(j) are disjoint for every pair of
distinct internal vertices i != j, where A(i) in {{i}, {i-1, i}}.

The only potential overlap occurs when one of the following holds:

(a) A(i) = {i} and A(j) = {j} with i = j. Excluded since i != j.

(b) A(i) = {i-1, i} and A(j) = {j} with j = i-1 or j = i.
    - j = i is excluded.
    - j = i-1: vertex i is Case LR (both children), so by Stanley's key
      structural observation (line 259, formalized as the precondition structure
      in M4_DESCENT_EFFECT_INFORMAL.md section 1.3): when vertex i has both
      children, vertex i-1 is the rightmost leaf of the left subtree of vertex
      i, hence an **endpoint**. Therefore psi_{i-1} = id and vertex i-1 is not
      an internal vertex. So j = i-1 cannot be an internal vertex, and this
      case does not arise.

(c) A(i) = {i} and A(j) = {j-1, j} with i = j-1 or i = j.
    Symmetric to (b): if j has both children, then j-1 is an endpoint, so
    i = j-1 cannot be internal.

(d) A(i) = {i-1, i} and A(j) = {j-1, j} with {i-1, i} intersect {j-1, j}
    nonempty.
    - If i = j, excluded.
    - If i = j-1: vertex j is Case LR, so j-1 = i is an endpoint. But then
      vertex i is not internal, contradiction.
    - If i-1 = j: vertex i is Case LR, so i-1 = j is an endpoint, contradiction.
    - If i-1 = j-1: then i = j, excluded.

In every case, we reach either a contradiction or the disjointness follows.
QED.

### 2.3 Consequence: factored action on descent sets

The disjointness of affected position sets means that the action of G_w on
descent sets **factors** as a product of independent toggles/swaps at
non-overlapping positions. Concretely, for any subset I of the internal
vertices and any position k in {0, ..., n-2}:

    is_descent(psi_I w, k) =
      if k is the "main position" of some unique internal vertex i in I:
        (descent bit toggled according to Case R or Case LR for i)
      else:
        is_descent(w, k).

This factorization is the heart of Fact #3.

---

## 3. The product formula

### 3.1 Ordering and notation

Order the internal vertices as i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_{iota} where
iota = iota(w). Let I = {i_1, ..., i_iota}. For a subset S of I, write

    psi_S = composition of psi_{i} for i in S

(order does not matter by commutativity). The M-equivalence class is

    [w] = { psi_S(w) : S subseteq I }.

### 3.2 Decomposition by vertex type

Group the positions 0, 1, ..., n-1 into three types:

- **Type-e positions** (endpoints): the set E = {0, ..., n-1} \ I. These have
  window_size = 1, so psi_i = id. The descent bit at each position k in
  {0, ..., n-2} that is "owned" only by an endpoint is constant across [w].

172	  with has_left_child i w = false. Each such i has A(i) = {i}, and psi_i
173	  toggles the descent bit at position i.
174	
175	- **Type-d positions** (both children): the set D_LR of internal vertices i
176	  with has_left_child i w = true. Each such i has A(i) = {i-1, i}, and psi_i
177	  swaps the descent bits at positions i-1 and i (toggling both).
178	
179	### 3.3 The sum as a product
180	
181	**Claim.**
182	
183	    Sum_{S subseteq I} u_{D(psi_S(w))}
184	      = Product over positions 0, ..., n-2 of (contributions)
185	
186	We decompose u_{D(v)} = e_0 e_1 ... e_{n-2} and factor the sum
187	over subsets S as a product over independent groups of positions.
188	
189	For each internal vertex i_j, define the **local contribution** when
190	i_j is or is not included in S:
191	
192	**Case c (right-child only, A(i) = {i}):**
193	
194	  - i not in S: descent bit at position i is is_descent(w, i). Contributes
195	    letter e_i = a (if not descent) or b (if descent).
196	  - i in S: descent bit toggles. Contributes the opposite letter.
197	  - Sum over {in, out}: e_i + e_i' = a + b, regardless of the initial state.
198	
199	**Case d (both children, A(i) = {i-1, i}):**
200	
201	  - i not in S: descent bits at i-1 and i are (d_{i-1}, d_i). By
202	    `exactly_one_descent_LR`, exactly one is a descent. So the pair of letters
203	    is either (a, b) or (b, a).
204	  - i in S: the bits swap, so the pair flips: (a, b) -> (b, a) or vice versa.
205	  - Sum over {in, out}: ab + ba, regardless of the initial state.
206	
207	  Note: position i-1 is an endpoint (Stanley line 259), so it has no
208	  independent toggle of its own. The pair {i-1, i} is "owned" entirely by
209	  vertex i.
210	
211	**Endpoints** contribute a fixed letter (a or b) that does not vary across [w].
212	
213	### 3.4 Assembly
214	
215	Now write the sum:
216	
217	    Sum_{S subseteq I} u_{D(psi_S(w))}
218	      = Sum_{S subseteq I} (e_0(S) e_1(S) ... e_{n-2}(S))
219	
220	where e_k(S) is the letter at position k for the permutation psi_S(w).
221	
222	Because the positions affected by different internal vertices are disjoint,
223	and the sum ranges over all 2^iota subsets (each internal vertex independently
224	in or out), the sum factors:
225	
226	    = [product over endpoint positions k not paired with any d-vertex]
227	      * [product over c-vertices i_j of (a + b)]
228	      * [product over d-vertices i_j of (ab + ba)]
229	
230	with the products taken in position order (left to right). The endpoint
231	positions contribute fixed letters, so they sit between the (a+b) and (ab+ba)
232	factors in the correct order.
233	
234	Formally, walk through positions k = 0, 1, ..., n-2:
235	
236	- If k is an endpoint position (not "owned" by any internal vertex):
237	  it contributes the fixed letter a or b.
238	- If k is the main position of a c-vertex: it contributes the factor (a + b).
239	- If k = i-1 for a d-vertex i: it contributes the first letter of (ab + ba).
240	  If k = i (the main position of a d-vertex): it contributes the second letter.
241	  Together the pair {i-1, i} contributes (ab + ba).
242	
243	Now delete the endpoint factors (replace e -> empty word). What remains is
244	exactly the product of (a + b) for each c-vertex and (ab + ba) for each

246	
247	    Phi_w(c := a + b, d := ab + ba).
248	
249	QED.

1	# Open axioms — status after M1–M7 iteration (2026-04-16)
2	
3	## Executive summary
4	
5	The original two axioms in `beta_swap.v` (`beta_swap_monotone_both_in`,
6	`beta_swap_lt_both_in`) have been **converted to lemmas**. They now derive
7	from two smaller, well-scoped axioms: `beta_swap_lt_caseA` and
8	`beta_swap_lt_caseB`. In addition, 22 axioms exist in `psi.v` supporting
9	the cd-index infrastructure (M2–M6). All are documented below with their
10	mathematical justification, non-triviality witnesses, and estimated
11	difficulty to close.
12	
13	**Bug fix (2026-04-16):** The original axioms toggled `i` (the lower
14	index), which is incorrect — counterexample: n=4, D={2,3}, β(D)=6 > 4 =
15	β(D\{2}). The correct formulation toggles `j` (the upper index).
16	Propagated through `beta_swap_monotone`, `beta_swap_lt`, and
17	`beta_alt_max_bounded`.

21	## 1. Target axioms in `beta_swap.v` (2 axioms)
22	
23	These are the only axioms that `beta_alt_max` (the project's end goal)
24	depends on.

26	### `beta_swap_lt_caseA` (line ~120)
27	
28	```coq
29	Axiom beta_swap_lt_caseA : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
30	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
31	  (forall q : 'I_n, val q = (val j).+1 -> q \in D) ->
32	  beta D < beta (toggle_at D j).
33	```
34	
35	**Meaning:** When both i, j=i+1 are descents AND the successor j+1 is
36	also in D (or j is at the boundary), toggling j strictly increases β.
37	
38	**Why true:** Under this hypothesis, `toggle_at_j_omega_strict_superset`
39	(proved in §H) gives ω(D) ⊊ ω(toggle_at D j). Prop 1.6.4 then gives
40	β(D) < β(toggle_at D j).
41	
42	**Gap to close:** The type bridge from `psi.v`'s seq-level `omega_seq` /
43	`fact3` / `strict_witness_exists` to `beta_swap.v`'s finset-level
44	`omega_set` / `beta`. Specifically:
45	- Define a bijection between `seq nat`-permutations and `{perm 'I_n.+1}`.
46	- Show `is_descent_seq w k ↔ is_descent (perm_of_seq w) k`.
47	- Show `omega_seq w = omega_set (descent_set (perm_of_seq w))` (under
48	  appropriate encoding).
49	- Connect `|{[w] : S_w ⊆ ω(S)}|` to `beta(S)` via the M-class counting.
50	
51	**Estimated difficulty:** Medium (~80 LOC). The math is done; this is
52	plumbing between two type universes.

54	### `beta_swap_lt_caseB` (line ~131)
55	
56	```coq
57	Axiom beta_swap_lt_caseB : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
58	  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
59	  (exists q : 'I_n, val q = (val j).+1 /\ q \notin D) ->
60	  beta D < beta (toggle_at D j).
61	```
62	
63	**Meaning:** When both i, j=i+1 are descents AND j+1 ∉ D (so the ω-sets
64	are incomparable — bit i enters, bit j leaves), toggling j still strictly
65	increases β.
66	
67	**Why true:** The cd-index coefficient structure guarantees that the
68	"marginal contribution" of ω-bit i exceeds that of ω-bit j = i+1 in the
69	expansion. Informally: gaining a lower-index ω-bit always compensates for
70	losing a higher-index one, because cd-monomials with d at position i are
71	a strict superset (in the ω-containment ordering) of those with d at
72	position j.

75	comparison lemma at the cd-index level. This requires showing that for
76	any cd-word Φ_w, if S_w ⊆ C ∪ {j} then S_w ⊆ C ∪ {i} (where C is the
77	common ω-bits), which follows from the structural constraint that d at
78	position j in the cde-string implies d at position i is "compatible".

# Open axioms — status after M1–M7 iteration (2026-04-16)

## Executive summary

The original two axioms in `beta_swap.v` (`beta_swap_monotone_both_in`,
`beta_swap_lt_both_in`) have been **converted to lemmas**. They now derive
from two smaller, well-scoped axioms: `beta_swap_lt_caseA` and
`beta_swap_lt_caseB`. In addition, 22 axioms exist in `psi.v` supporting
the cd-index infrastructure (M2–M6). All are documented below with their
mathematical justification, non-triviality witnesses, and estimated
difficulty to close.

**Bug fix (2026-04-16):** The original axioms toggled `i` (the lower
index), which is incorrect — counterexample: n=4, D={2,3}, β(D)=6 > 4 =
β(D\{2}). The correct formulation toggles `j` (the upper index).
Propagated through `beta_swap_monotone`, `beta_swap_lt`, and
`beta_alt_max_bounded`.

---

## 1. Target axioms in `beta_swap.v` (2 axioms)

These are the only axioms that `beta_alt_max` (the project's end goal)
depends on.

### `beta_swap_lt_caseA` (line ~120)

```coq
Axiom beta_swap_lt_caseA : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  (forall q : 'I_n, val q = (val j).+1 -> q \in D) ->
  beta D < beta (toggle_at D j).
```

**Meaning:** When both i, j=i+1 are descents AND the successor j+1 is
also in D (or j is at the boundary), toggling j strictly increases β.

**Why true:** Under this hypothesis, `toggle_at_j_omega_strict_superset`
(proved in §H) gives ω(D) ⊊ ω(toggle_at D j). Prop 1.6.4 then gives
β(D) < β(toggle_at D j).

**Gap to close:** The type bridge from `psi.v`'s seq-level `omega_seq` /
`fact3` / `strict_witness_exists` to `beta_swap.v`'s finset-level
`omega_set` / `beta`. Specifically:
- Define a bijection between `seq nat`-permutations and `{perm 'I_n.+1}`.
- Show `is_descent_seq w k ↔ is_descent (perm_of_seq w) k`.
- Show `omega_seq w = omega_set (descent_set (perm_of_seq w))` (under
  appropriate encoding).
- Connect `|{[w] : S_w ⊆ ω(S)}|` to `beta(S)` via the M-class counting.

**Estimated difficulty:** Medium (~80 LOC). The math is done; this is
plumbing between two type universes.

### `beta_swap_lt_caseB` (line ~131)

```coq
Axiom beta_swap_lt_caseB : forall n (D : {set 'I_n}) (i j : 'I_n),
  val j = (val i).+1 -> i \in D -> j \in D ->
  (exists q : 'I_n, val q = (val j).+1 /\ q \notin D) ->
  beta D < beta (toggle_at D j).
```

**Meaning:** When both i, j=i+1 are descents AND j+1 ∉ D (so the ω-sets
are incomparable — bit i enters, bit j leaves), toggling j still strictly
increases β.

**Why true:** The cd-index coefficient structure guarantees that the
"marginal contribution" of ω-bit i exceeds that of ω-bit j = i+1 in the
expansion. Informally: gaining a lower-index ω-bit always compensates for
losing a higher-index one, because cd-monomials with d at position i are
a strict superset (in the ω-containment ordering) of those with d at
position j.

**Gap to close:** Same type bridge as Case A, PLUS a marginal-contribution
comparison lemma at the cd-index level. This requires showing that for
any cd-word Φ_w, if S_w ⊆ C ∪ {j} then S_w ⊆ C ∪ {i} (where C is the
common ω-bits), which follows from the structural constraint that d at
position j in the cde-string implies d at position i is "compatible".

**Estimated difficulty:** Hard (~60 LOC for the marginal lemma + ~80 LOC
for the type bridge shared with Case A). The mathematical argument is in
M7_CLOSING_AXIOMS_INFORMAL.md §4.5.

---

## 2. Infrastructure axioms in `psi.v` (22 axioms)

Grouped by milestone. Each has a non-triviality `Example` in `psi.v`.

### M2: ψᵢ involutivity (1 axiom)

| Axiom | Line | Difficulty | Gap |
|-------|------|------------|-----|
| `psi_involutive` | 594 | **Hard** | Shape stability: `mm_pos` is preserved under `psi`. See M2_SUBTASKS.md T4–T5. Decomposed into `window_head_extremum` + `psi_window_shape_stable` + assembly. ~135 LOC. Three agent runs attempted; scaffolding (`rank_shift_seq_involutive`) proved, shape stability unfinished. |

### M3: ψᵢ commutativity (4 axioms)

| Axiom | Line | Difficulty | Gap |
|-------|------|------------|-----|
| `window_trichotomy` | 639 | Easy | Structural property of binary trees: subtrees disjoint or nested. ~15 LOC by induction on tree. |
| `psi_comm_disjoint` | 663 | Medium | Disjoint windows act on non-overlapping slices. ~30 LOC. Blocked on T4–T5 (window stability). |
| `window_size_psi_ancestor` | 687 | Medium | Window-size stable when ancestor window is rank-shifted. ~25 LOC. Blocked on T4. |
| `psi_comm_nested` | 714 | Medium | Nested windows: RS commutes by modular arithmetic. ~30 LOC. Core algebra is straightforward; blocked on window stability. |

### M4: Descent-set effect (10 axioms)

| Axiom | Line | Difficulty | Gap |
|-------|------|------------|-----|
| `rank_shift_preserves_interior_order` | 855 | Medium | Interior (non-head) elements preserve relative order under rank-shift. ~20 LOC. Modular arithmetic. |
| `window_head_is_extremum` | 877 | Medium | Head of non-trivial window is min or max (F2 property). ~30 LOC by induction on size. Proved once (lost to backup error). |
| `post_window_extremum` | 896 | Medium | Element after window is outside window's range. ~25 LOC. Tree-structural. |
| `pre_window_lt_max_when_min_head` | 916 | Medium | Case LR boundary: w[i-1] < max(window). ~20 LOC. |
| `pre_window_gt_min_when_max_head` | 922 | Medium | Symmetric to above. ~20 LOC. |
| `exactly_one_descent_LR` | 941 | Medium | XOR of descents at {i-1, i} in Case LR. ~25 LOC. |
| `descent_psi_R_add` | 961 | Medium | Case R, not a descent → becomes descent. ~20 LOC. Follows from head-extremum flip. |
| `descent_psi_R_remove` | 968 | Medium | Case R, is a descent → removed. ~20 LOC. Symmetric. |
| `descent_psi_LR_swap1` | 975 | Medium | Case LR swap (i ∉ D). ~25 LOC. |
| `descent_psi_LR_swap2` | 985 | Medium | Case LR swap (i ∈ D). ~25 LOC. |

### M5: Fact #3 — cd-index identity (5 axioms)

| Axiom | Line | Difficulty | Gap |
|-------|------|------------|-----|
| `window_size_psi` | 1145 | Medium | Tree shape invariant: `window_size i (psi j w) = window_size i w`. ~30 LOC. Same blocker as M2 T5. |
| `has_left_child_psi` | 1164 | Medium | Tree shape invariant: `has_left_child` stable under psi. ~20 LOC. |
| `endpoint_implies_next_has_left_child` | 1181 | Easy | Structural: endpoint k < n-1 ⟹ k+1 has left child. ~15 LOC. |
| `LR_pred_is_endpoint` | 1203 | Easy | If vertex i is Case LR, then i-1 is endpoint. ~15 LOC. Stanley line 259. |
| `fact3` | 1241 | **Hard** | The main Fact #3 identity. Requires induction on |internal_vertices| using M4 descent-effect axioms + independence of disjoint bit-operations. ~100 LOC once M4 axioms are closed. |

### M6: Theorem 1.6.3 assembly (2 axioms)

| Axiom | Line | Difficulty | Gap |
|-------|------|------------|-----|
| `phi_w_support` | 1360 | Medium | Φ_w support characterization: X ∈ expand(Φ_w) ↔ S_w ⊆ ω(X). ~40 LOC. Combinatorial identity on cd-expansion. |
| `strict_witness_exists` | 1417 | Easy | For any k < n-1, ∃ w with S_w = {k}. ~15 LOC. Construct explicit permutation c^{k} d c^{n-2-k}. |

---

## 3. Dependency graph (what blocks what)

```
psi_involutive (M2, HARD)
  └── blocks: psi_comm_disjoint (M3)
  └── blocks: window stability axioms (M3, M5)

window_head_is_extremum (M4)
  └── blocks: descent_psi_* axioms (M4)
  └── blocks: fact3 (M5)

fact3 (M5, HARD)
  └── blocks: phi_w_support (M6)
  └── blocks: beta_swap_lt_caseA (M7)
  └── blocks: beta_swap_lt_caseB (M7)

TYPE BRIDGE (seq nat ↔ {perm 'I_n.+1})
  └── blocks: beta_swap_lt_caseA (M7)
  └── blocks: beta_swap_lt_caseB (M7)
```

**Critical path:** `psi_involutive` → window stability → M4 descent axioms
→ `fact3` → type bridge → close `beta_swap_lt_caseA/B`.

---

## 4. Recommended attack order for next iteration

### Phase 1: Close the shape-stability bottleneck (~135 LOC)

This unblocks everything. Follow M2_SUBTASKS.md:
1. **T4: `mm_pos_stable`** (~40 LOC) — the mathematical crux.
2. **T5: `window_stable`** (~50 LOC) — window_size and window_at preserved.
3. **T6: `window_head_extremum`** (~30 LOC) — independent, can run in parallel.
4. **T7: `psi_involutive` assembly** (~15 LOC).

Once T4–T5 land, the following axioms fall like dominoes:
- `psi_involutive` (M2)
- `window_size_psi`, `has_left_child_psi` (M5)
- `window_trichotomy`, `psi_comm_disjoint`, `window_size_psi_ancestor`,
  `psi_comm_nested` (M3)

### Phase 2: Close M4 descent-effect axioms (~230 LOC)

All 10 M4 axioms depend on `window_head_is_extremum` (closed in Phase 1)
plus straightforward rank-shift algebra. Each is ~20–25 LOC.

### Phase 3: Close Fact #3 and M6 (~155 LOC)

- `endpoint_implies_next_has_left_child` (~15 LOC, easy)
- `LR_pred_is_endpoint` (~15 LOC, easy)
- `fact3` (~100 LOC, hard — induction on internal vertices)
- `phi_w_support` (~40 LOC)
- `strict_witness_exists` (~15 LOC, easy — explicit construction)

### Phase 4: Type bridge + close target axioms (~160 LOC)

- Define `seq_of_perm : {perm 'I_n.+1} -> seq nat` and inverse.
- Bridge `is_descent_seq ↔ is_descent`, `omega_seq ↔ omega_set`.
- Bridge M-class counting to `beta`.
- Close `beta_swap_lt_caseA` and `beta_swap_lt_caseB`.

### Total remaining: ~680 LOC across 4 phases.

---

## 5. Don't-repeat-these-mistakes log

Documented failure modes from prior agent rounds:

1. **`2*i` indexing for internal vertices.** The i-th label in the in-order
   word of M(w) is at position `i`, not `2i`.

2. **Packaged-hypothesis "bridges."** Defining
   `tree_well_c_at t i := is_node_c ∧ seq_type_c_at` and declaring the
   bridge closed. The bridge is the *implication*, not the conjunction.

3. **`psi_stanley := psi` as an alias** without genuine operator content.

4. **`psi := id` as a "scaffold".** Involutivity and commutation hold
   trivially; the operator does nothing.

5. **Toggling the wrong index.** The original axioms toggled `i` (lower
   descent); the correct formulation toggles `j = i+1` (upper descent).
   Counterexample: n=4, D={2,3}, toggle i=2: β goes from 6 to 4 (DOWN).
   Toggle j=3: β goes from 6 to 9 (UP).

6. **Agent backup-restore errors.** One agent proved `window_head_extremum`
   and several shape-stability helpers (~180 LOC) but lost all work by
   restoring from a stale backup. Keep incremental saves or use
   `rocq_compile_file` after each completed lemma.

7. **Shape stability is the bottleneck.** Three agents attempted
   `psi_involutive` end-to-end without success. The correct decomposition

(* psi.v — Milestone 2: Stanley's operators ψᵢ on min-max trees             *)
(*                                                                           *)
(* Implements the rank-shift operators ψᵢ of Stanley EC1 §1.6.3 on sequences *)
(* of distinct integers, with the min-or-max alternating tree construction   *)
(* (Option A of M2_PSI_INFORMAL.md §1.3).                                    *)

From mathcomp Require Import all_ssreflect.
Require Import mmtree.

Set Implicit Arguments.
Unset Strict Implicit.
Unset Printing Implicit Defensive.

(* ----- 1. Alternating min-or-max split ----------------------------------- *)

Definition max_pos (s : seq nat) : nat :=
  index (foldr maxn (head 0 s) (behead s)) s.

Definition mm_pos (s : seq nat) : nat :=
  if min_pos s <= max_pos s then min_pos s else max_pos s.

Lemma max_in s a : foldr maxn a s \in a :: s.
Proof.
elim: s a => [| b s IH] a /=.
  by rewrite inE eqxx.
rewrite !inE.
case: leqP => _.
  have := IH a; rewrite inE => /orP [->|->] //; by rewrite !orbT.
by rewrite eqxx orbT.
Qed.

all (fun k => k \in omega_seq T) (S_w_seq w).
Proof.
move=> _ _ Hsub w _ _ /allP Hall.
by apply/allP => k Hk; apply: Hsub; apply: Hall.
Qed.

(* Strict witness: for any k, the cd-word c^k d c^{m-k} has S_w = {k}.
   Therefore if k ∈ ω(T)\ω(S), there is a class contributing to β(T) but
   not β(S). This is Stanley's argument (line 394-395). *)
Axiom strict_witness_exists : forall (n : nat) (k : nat),
  k < n.-1 ->
  exists w : seq nat,
    uniq w /\ size w = n /\ S_w_seq w = [:: k].

(* Non-triviality: for k = 0, n = 3, w = [2;1;3] has S_w = {0}. *)
Example strict_witness_ex1 :
  S_w_seq [:: 2; 1; 3] = [:: 0].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

(* For k = 1, n = 4, w = [1;3;2;4] has S_w = {1}. *)
Example strict_witness_ex2 :
  S_w_seq [:: 1; 3; 2; 4] = [:: 1].
Proof. by native_compute. Qed.

  S_w_seq [:: 2; 1; 3; 4; 5] = [:: 0].

```coq
Axiom strict_witness_exists : forall (n : nat) (k : nat),
  k < n.-2 ->
  exists w : seq nat,
    uniq w /\ size w = n /\ S_w_seq w = [:: k].
```

Note: the bound was just fixed from `k < n.-1` to `k < n.-2` because the last position of a sequence is always a leaf (window_size = 1), so it can never be a D-letter.

### Definitions
```coq
Definition S_w_seq (w : seq nat) : seq nat :=
  [seq i.-1 | i <- iota 1 (size w).-1
             & is_D_letter (classify_vertex_cde i w)].

Definition classify_vertex_cde (i : nat) (w : seq nat) : cde :=
  if ~~ is_internal i w then E_letter
  else if has_left_child i w then D_letter
  else C_letter.

Definition is_internal (i : nat) (w : seq nat) : bool :=
  (i < size w) && (1 < window_size i w).

(* has_left_child uses has_left_child_fuel which recurses via mm_pos *)
```

### Mathematical idea
For any k < n-2, construct a witness permutation w of [1..n] with S_w_seq w = [:: k].

The witness: `w = iota 1 k ++ [:: k+2; k+1] ++ iota (k+3) (n-k-2)`

This is the sequence `[1; 2; ...; k; k+2; k+1; k+3; k+4; ...; n]`.
